Solve ordinary differential equations

Source: R/solvers-ode-ode.R
dsolve.Rd

dsolve(eq, func) solves the ordinary differential equation eq (an expression taken equal to zero, or an Eq()) for the unknown function func, as SymPy's dsolve(). The hints of classify_ode() are tried in SymPy's order; hint names one of them, or the meta hints "default", "all", "all_Integral" and "best". A list of equations is solved as a system of ODEs.

Usage

dsolve(
  eq,
  func = NULL,
  hint = "default",
  simplify = TRUE,
  ics = NULL,
  xi = NULL,
  eta = NULL,
  x0 = 0,
  n = 6,
  ...
)

Arguments

eq

The equation, or a list of equations for a system.

func

The unknown function such as f(x), or a list of functions for a system; detected from the equation when NULL.

hint

The solution method.

simplify

Whether to simplify the solution with odesimp().

ics

Initial conditions: a list of pairs list(f(x0), value) or list(Subs(Derivative(f(x), x, n), x, x0), value); the triple form list(x0, n, value) is accepted too.

xi, eta

Infinitesimals for the lie_group hint.

x0

The point of expansion for the power series hints.

n

The number of power series terms.

...

Further options passed on to the hints.

Value

An equation, or a list of equations; a named list for the "all" hints.

Examples

x <- Symbol("x"); f <- Function("f")
dsolve(Derivative(f(x), x, 2) - 3 * Derivative(f(x), x) + 2 * f(x), f(x))
#> Eq(f(x), (C1 + C2*exp(x))*exp(x))
dsolve(Derivative(f(x), x) - f(x), f(x), ics = list(list(f(0), 1)))
#> Eq(f(x), exp(x))
